progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: s01 (the reading routine and the annotation layer). Biology: B10 (sex chromosomes; a gene on the X has no partner on the Y; sons get their X from their mother), B4 (template strands, complementary base pairing). Chemistry: C1 (soda water; open against closed systems; dissolving and leaving rates), C3 (the iron thiocyanate tube and its added-Fe3+ case, in scene 9).
progression.startsWith: Three verbs that look alike. The video opens: In the last five years of HSC Chemistry and Biology papers, one key word came up in the written section more than any other: explain. Fifty-seven question parts, more than twice as many as the next word. Most were worth two to four marks.
progression.stopsAfter: answering one stimulus at three verb levels, and the s01 iron thiocyanate case at three levels; building a three-point explanation with linked causes; spotting a description posing as an explanation; two explain drills.
progression.nextLesson: s03, compare and contrast (similarities and differences written as pairs).

teaching.task: Identify, describe and explain look alike. What does each one ask you to write, and how do you know you've actually explained?
teaching.causalExplanation: (1) explain is the commonest HSC key word, and NESA marking feedback flags outcomes stated without the causal link every year (1); (2) the three verbs with their paraphrased glossary meanings, read in the context of the question (2); (3) one fruit fly reciprocal-cross stimulus with three lettered parts holds the content still (3); (4) identify names (4); (5) describe gives features (5); (6) explain asks how or why, so the cause is set up first (6); (7) a three-point chain in which each sentence says what causes what (7); (8) a description that contains "because" is still not an explanation (8); (9) the same three verbs on the s01 Chemistry case (9); (10) the how test: does each sentence say what causes what? (10); two explain drills with feedback (11 to 14); decision rule and handoff (15); key notes (16).
teaching.conversationalApproach: identify, describe and explain look alike, so one stimulus (a fruit fly reciprocal cross) holds the content still while the verb changes: identify names, describe gives features, explain links each cause to the next. A weak answer that contains "because" shows a description posing as an explanation, the s01 Chemistry case gets the same three-verb ladder for Chemistry viewers, and the how test gives the check. Two explain drills, one per subject, follow.
teaching.openingDecision: In the last five years of HSC Chemistry and Biology papers, one key word came up in the written section more than any other: explain. Fifty-seven question parts, more than twice as many as the next word. Most were worth two to four marks. And every year, NESA's marking feedback mentions answers that say what happens, but not why. So let's sort out three verbs that look alike, but ask for different things.
teaching.understandingCheck: both are explain, the verb that needs practice. The narration says "Do the one in your subject, or both". Drill 1, Chemistry, 3 marks: soda water opened. The content is C1's open-bottle framing. Crossed habit: "bubbles form because gas comes out of the drink" (describes the bubbles). Drill 2, Biology, 2 marks (explain's second commonest value): why the two DNA molecules from replication are identical. The content is B4. The condition "assume no copying errors" is on the card. Crossed habit: "because each has one old strand and one new strand" (describes the result, gives no cause of the matching sequence).
teaching.curriculumScope: No syllabus dotpoint (skills video, HSC exam skills series): the NESA glossary of key words (paraphrased) and the Working Scientifically skill Communicating (NSW Chemistry and Biology Stage 6 syllabuses, 2017). starts at "three verbs that look alike". It stops after the meaning of identify, describe and explain (outline in passing), the cause-and-effect link, the "how" test, a weak against strong explain, and two explain drills. It does not cover compare, contrast or distinguish (s03), judgement verbs (s04), calculations (s05) or data descriptions in depth (s06).

design.visualSystem: Explainer engine: warm paper stage, handwritten Caveat headings, amber doodle layer. s01's shared components (`QuestionCard` with its annotation layer, `AnswerBox`, `MarkCounter`, `RoutineStrip` small at the far left, `LostMarksTag`). New for this video: a verb ladder, three stacked rungs (identify, describe, explain), each with a depth icon: identify: one word chip; describe: a feature list; explain: a chain of cause box, "so" arrow, effect box. New: a cause-effect chain overlay that draws arrows between linked clauses in the answer box, with "because" and "so" underlined amber. B10's `SexChrom` X and Y chips for the explain build. No people, hands or faces.
design.transitionPlan: The hook opens on the frequency card; the verb ladder builds three rungs with depth icons; the fly question card writes with its three lettered parts; each part fills its answer box in turn while its rung lights; the cause-effect chain overlay draws arrows between linked clauses; the weak answer box slides in beside the strong one; the Chemistry ladder appears as one compact scene; each drill clears the board and its feedback annotates the card before the model answer writes with ticks; the decision rule card and next chip close; scene crossfade with settle.
